notes: Endpoint: amazon.jobs is a Rails app whose search page XHRs GET /en/search.json; plain httpx with the replay UA gets HTTP 200, no cookies/headers needed. Top-level `hits` is the site-claimed total for the filtered query; `jobs` is the page of records.

WHY pagination style=none despite the endpoint supporting offset/result_limit: replay.py passes pagination params via httpx `params=`, and httpx 0.28 REPLACES the URL's entire query string with them — every filter (base_query, city, ...) would be dropped and the scrape would silently become the global amazon.jobs firehose (verified: hits jumped 76 -> 10000). POST with a JSON body is rejected (422, Rails CSRF). So the recipe bakes result_limit=100 (the server-enforced max; >100 returns HTTP 200 with error='Result limit cannot be greater than 100' and jobs=null, which replay fails loudly on) into the URL and fetches once.

CONSEQUENCE / known fragility: if this filtered search ever exceeds 100 open jobs, the recipe returns exactly the first 100 SILENTLY (sort=recent, so the newest 100). At discovery time hits=76 of 76 replayed — full coverage. See FINDINGS.md SCHEMA GAP for the fix (compare replayed count to `hits`).

id = id_icims (the requisition number that appears in the public job URL and apply URL, e.g. 10490514); the `uuid` field keeps the search-index document id. Both were non-null on all 76 records at discovery.
posted_date is a US long-form date with a padded double space for single-digit days ('August  3, 2026') — parse with a whitespace-tolerant format, not a strict '%B %d, %Y'.

expected_min_jobs=20: this query (software engineer within 24km of Austin, an AWS hub) held 76 open reqs at discovery; below 20 means the endpoint semantics, filter parsing, or Amazon's Austin presence changed — a human should look either way.
